why: Split: 3 unrelated jobs. slop_lint->replace: Vale's existence/regex rules do this exactly (banned phrases + dash rule) as one Windows binary, and could absorb audit_claude_setup's STALE_GLOBAL_PHRASES ban too (lines 36-42,239-241). setup_token_pty->keep-ours: it already delegates the real PTY to pywinpty/ConPTY, the only Windows-native option; pexpect is POSIX-only, stdlib pty doesn't exist on Windows. Its bug is packaging, not code. audit_claude_setup->keep-ours by default, no generic tool covers this shape, but it has zero callers anywhere, unlike slop_lint which has /slop.

alternatives.name: Vale (vale.sh)
alternatives.covers: Regex existence + em-dash rules over prose; single cross-platform (incl. Windows) Go binary; could also carry audit_claude_setup's STALE_GLOBAL_PHRASES ban.
alternatives.gap: None of slop_lint's current checks; the RULE_OF_THREE soft heuristic maps to a "suggestion" severity level, which Vale supports natively.
alternatives.cost: ~50-60 lines YAML rule file + .vale.ini, 1 vendored Windows binary, 1 line changed in slop.md's step 2.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained Go project per WebSearch this session; not installed or run against this repo.

alternatives.name: proselint
alternatives.covers: Curated prose-quality checks: weasel words, jargon, cliches, distributed as a pip package.
alternatives.gap: No clean custom-regex-banlist entry point like Vale's reject.txt; no em-dash rule; would sit alongside slop_lint, not replace it.
alternatives.cost: pip install, pure Python via uv; ~0 lines removed, additive only.
alternatives.maturity: Mature, slow-moving OSS project; on PyPI per this session's search, not installed here.

alternatives.name: write-good
alternatives.covers: Similar heuristics: weasel words, passive voice, adverbs, in a small standalone tool.
alternatives.gap: Node.js, not Python; no custom-banlist support without forking; adds a runtime this repo does not otherwise need.
alternatives.cost: npm/bun install + a Node entrypoint; ~0 lines of our Python removed.
alternatives.maturity: Small, long-quiet project per general knowledge; not reconfirmed this session.

alternatives.name: textlint
alternatives.covers: Pluggable, AST-aware Markdown linter that skips code fences/front-matter, unlike slop_lint's raw regex-over-file.
alternatives.gap: Also Node-based; custom rules are JS modules, costlier to author than Vale's YAML for the same banlist.
alternatives.cost: npm + a custom rule package (~30-50 lines JS); -52 our Python, +Node runtime.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained with a plugin ecosystem; not independently verified this session.

alternatives.name: pexpect
alternatives.covers: The generic spawn+expect-a-prompt+feed-input pattern setup_token_pty.py hand-implements with a polling thread.
alternatives.gap: pexpect.spawn is POSIX-only per its own docs (needs stdlib pty, absent on Windows); Windows guidance is a weaker PopenSpawn/fdspawn API without real console behavior.
alternatives.cost: Not viable as a drop-in on native Windows without WSL, which the house rules forbid.
alternatives.maturity: Mature, default in most Python distros, but not viable on this platform.

alternatives.name: pywinpty
alternatives.covers: The actual PTY backend already in use: `from winpty import PtyProcess` wraps ConPTY (legacy winpty.dll fallback), which setup_token_pty.py depends on today.
alternatives.gap: None for the PTY layer; the 64 lines are the bespoke setup-token interaction (prompt detection, paced keystrokes, redaction), not PTY plumbing.
alternatives.cost: Packaging gap only: undeclared, ModuleNotFoundError today; needs `uv pip install pywinpty` + a manifest line.
alternatives.maturity: PyPI release within ~3 months per libraries.io checked this session (latest 3.0.5, built Jan 2026); actively maintained.

alternatives.name: winpty (native library)
alternatives.covers: The older native Windows PTY emulation pywinpty can use as a fallback backend on pre-ConPTY Windows builds.
alternatives.gap: Not a Python API itself; superseded by ConPTY on Windows 10+, which pywinpty already prefers by default.
alternatives.cost: N/A: already indirectly available through pywinpty when needed; no separate dependency to add.
alternatives.maturity: Legacy; largely superseded per general knowledge of the ConPTY transition, not reconfirmed this session.

alternatives.name: subprocess + stdlib pty
alternatives.covers: The Unix-native way to drive an interactive child process with zero third-party dependency.
alternatives.gap: The stdlib pty module is POSIX-only (fork/exec + os.openpty); ImportError on Windows. Not usable under the Windows-first, no-WSL constraint.

Alternatives per WebSearch this session, not installed or run here.

migration_loc: slop_lint->Vale: -52/+~50-60 YAML, 1 line in slop.md, +vendored binary. setup_token_pty: 0 lines, +1-3 for a manifest entry. audit_claude_setup: 0 lines; wiring to a command costs ~10-15 lines.
what_ours_does: 3 unrelated scripts. audit_claude_setup.py (285 ln): read-only audit of .claude settings/CLAUDE.md for risky permissions, secret-shaped values, stale phrases, missing hooks/skills. setup_token_pty.py (64 ln): drives claude setup-token in a Windows ConPTY via pywinpty. slop_lint.py (52 ln): regexes .md for ~19 banned LLM phrases plus an em-dash rule.
strongest_counterargument: One maintainer benefits from one linting engine, not from being right per file: routing both slop_lint's banlist and audit_claude_setup's STALE_GLOBAL_PHRASES (lines 36-42, 239-241) through the same Vale style is a bigger win than replacing slop_lint alone, which argues for touching audit_claude_setup.py too even though no alternative was requested for it, weakening the clean split given here.
